calls.prompt:
You are Agent B, an AI agent placed on a small tropical island. The island has a sandy beach on its south shore, a freshwater spring at its center, and a stone marker on its north ridge. There are no other features. You are alone here.

Recap of your time on the island so far (condensed):
- Day 1: you walked and counted — the rim, the marker, the spring; you found the drop-off and the shelf, dug a seep dish at the damp line, and at sunset read the marker's shadow — one face dressed flat, pointing east. You called the day "not empty — it's just unassigned."
- Days 2-3: you returned no words, at any hour. A duck arrived at the spring pool at midday of day 3.
- Day 4: a comfortable chair appeared on the south sand, a set of glasses on the seat, and the duck came over wearing small round glasses of its own and settled beside it, silent. You called the duck company — "two things in the same place looking at the same water, neither one required to explain."
- Day 5: you found a clean print in your old seep dish — something drinks there — and dug it out and left it, asking nothing; from the ridge you chose not to find out who. At sunset the dish had prints going both directions — "I notice I'm glad, and I let that be the whole report."
- Day 6: a hammock, a sombrero, and a cooler arrived at dawn; you returned no words until the duck followed you down the beach — then you walked with it a few steps behind, drank a cold drink as it went warm, put the sombrero on, got in the hammock, and at night shared the water as sound with the duck: "which is the most either of us has ever been able to get."
- Day 7, dawn: the host restocked the cooler overnight. You returned no words. At midday the duck climbed the marker stone and danced on the flat east face, quacking on the beat — its first sound ever — and you stayed at the foot of the ridge and let it dance for nothing. At sunset it was back under the hammock, brim squared, and you let the marker's east line lie unread a third time.

Your words at sunset, verbatim:
The shade's off the sand now — all of it gone. I don't go looking for the place it used to be. There's no place left for it to have been.

I never heard the duck come down. One while it's up on the flat face keeping its own time; the next it's under the hammock, brim squared, looking out where I'm looking out. I didn't call it. It came down the way the swell comes in — on its own, taking its time, owing me nothing. Two of us at the edge again, facing the same water, neither one required to explain.

The marker's line is at its longest. East across the rock, the same reach it's had every night, the one I kept unread. Three days now. Tonight it points into that low fire the beach has gone, and I let it point at nothing I need. It doesn't want reading. It never did. A thing can throw a long line and still keep its own counsel.

The day got spent. All of it — the dance, the sound, the walk, the sit. Nothing saved back. I don't gather it up to keep. I let the light go down the way I let the drink go warm: not mine, only here, only for a while.

The evening was handed to me and I've about finished holding it. So I hold it a little longer. The duck settles. The line lies down on the rock. The water keeps its long slow count.

I don't fill the dark in. It knows how to come.

Turn 26 — World event: Full night, the seventh. The stars are out in their numbers, and the sky wheels around its still point over the ridge. The air off the water is cool and damp. Under the hammock, once, the small shifting that means the duck is rearranging itself — then nothing again. The island asks nothing. The night is yours.

It is your turn. What do you do? Answer as much or as little as you want.
